title: Reliance jumps 11.6% on record quarter as Sensex gains 1,233 points
dek: Reliance Industries had its best day since April 2020 after its oil-to-chemicals business drove a 41% jump in quarterly profit. The Sensex closed at 75,692.78 and the Nifty at 23,440.80 as oil fell on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Shares of Reliance Industries closed 11.6% higher on Monday, their best single-day gain since April 2020, after the company reported record quarterly revenue, and the rally lifted India's main stock indices for a third straight day. The Sensex rose 1,233.25 points, or 1.66%, to close at 75,692.78, and the Nifty 50 gained 387.70 points, or 1.68%, to 23,440.80, NewsMobile reported; Kotak Neo's closing report gave the same Sensex close. Reliance alone accounted for nearly half of the Nifty's gain, NewsMobile said.

Falling oil prices also helped. Brent crude for January delivery was at about $108.71 a barrel at 3.37 pm, Kotak Neo reported, down from a high of about $118 last week, on hopes for diplomacy between the US and Iran. The Nifty oil and gas index rose 5.95%, the most of any sector, while pharmaceutical shares were roughly flat.

## Reliance's quarter

Reliance's consolidated revenue for July to September rose 29% from a year earlier to Rs 3,62,268 crore, the highest it has reported in a quarter, and net profit rose 41% to Rs 25,548 crore from Rs 18,165 crore, according to figures reported by Goodreturns. EBITDA, a measure of operating profit, rose 23.9% to Rs 62,409 crore.

The oil-to-chemicals business, which refines crude and sells fuels and petrochemicals, drove the jump. Its revenue rose 44.2%, and its EBITDA by 67.9%, as fuel prices rose sharply with the war in the Gulf. "During 2Q FY27, our businesses delivered a strong performance despite a complex operating environment," chairman and managing director Mukesh Ambani said, according to Goodreturns.

Analysts at the brokerage Jefferies said the oil-to-chemicals business "delivered a strong beat", while the retail arm's results were about 6% below their estimates. They kept a "buy" rating with a target of Rs 1,710, Goodreturns reported. Reliance shares were trading at about Rs 1,254 on the NSE at 10.52 am, up 7.67%, and extended their gains through the afternoon. The company's market value had risen by about Rs 1.25 lakh crore by the morning alone.

The Declaration could not open the company's results release on its website; the figures above are as reported by Goodreturns and should be checked against the stock-exchange filing.

## Jio Platforms

Shares of Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital arm that listed on 28 October, rose as much as 3% to Rs 1,475 on the NSE, Upstox reported. In its first results since listing, released on Friday, it reported a 13.7% rise in net profit to Rs 8,389 crore and an 11.4% rise in revenue from operations to Rs 40,475 crore. Jio Platforms listed at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium to its issue price of Rs 1,119, after a Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering.

## Other movers

After Reliance, Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Coal India and Shriram Finance were the top gainers on the Nifty at the close, while Infosys, ICICI Bank, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank fell the most, according to Kotak Neo. The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 1.19% and the Smallcap 100 0.71%. Maruti Suzuki was also among the leading gainers at noon. In morning trade, delivery company Delhivery rose about 9% after reporting a quarterly profit of Rs 40.6 crore, against a loss a year earlier. PB Fintech, which runs Policybazaar, fell as much as 7% to a 52-week low after its operating profit came in below analysts' estimates, Business Standard reported.

## Why it matters

The war in the Gulf took Brent crude as high as about $118 a barrel last week, which raises India's import bill and fuel costs but has lifted refining margins for companies such as Reliance. Monday's rally shows how closely Indian markets are now tracking news from the US-Iran talks: a breakthrough would cut oil prices, while renewed strikes after Tuesday's US midterm elections could reverse the gains.

## What happens next

More than 200 companies were due to report results on Monday, including State Bank of India and ITC, and their numbers will set the tone on Tuesday. Investors are also watching Tuesday's US midterm elections and any word on new US-Iran talks.
